title: Getting started with lagprotest
text: PROTEST (Jackson 1995; Peres-Neto Jackson 2001) measures well two multivariate configurations observations match Procrustes superimposition, tests match permutation. observations ordered time points, example monthly means set environmental variables set phenotypic traits, concordance may strongest contemporaneous rows delay: response may track driver lag k time units. lagged_protest() asks lag two series match best. candidate lag k, row t X paired row t + k Y, series truncated n - k overlapping rows, symmetric Procrustes statistic m² computed. Lower m² means stronger concordance. lag tested permutation, lag smallest m² reported together full lag profile.

title: Getting started with lagprotest
text: Standard PROTEST permutes rows freely, assumes time points exchangeable null hypothesis. Seasonal otherwise autocorrelated series : two independent series cycle annually often look concordant null destroys temporal structure, problem shared permutation tests autocorrelated data (Legendre et al. 2002). lagged_protest() therefore defaults permutation = "cyclic". full Y series cyclically shifted 1, …, n − 1 positions, also time-reversed mirror = TRUE, lag applied. permuted series keeps autocorrelation. shifts enumerated, test exact needs random seed. permutation = "free" reproduces behavior vegan::protest() (Oksanen et al. 2026). difference matters. independence, small simulation 12 monthly samples gives: Rejection rates stay near nominal 0.05 cyclic shifts approach 1 free permutation.
code: reject <- function(permutation, n_rep) {   rates <- rowMeans(vapply(seq_len(n_rep), function(i) {     s <- simulate_lagged_series(n_times = 12, autocorr = 0, noise_sd = 0.3,                                 seed = i)     fit <- lagged_protest(s$X, s$Y, lags = 0:3, permutation = permutation,                           nperm = 99, seed = i)     fit$profile$p.value < 0.05   }, logical(4)))   setNames(rates, paste("lag", 0:3)) } rbind(cyclic = reject("cyclic", 100), free = reject("free", 50)) #>        lag 0 lag 1 lag 2 lag 3 #> cyclic  0.06  0.06  0.02  0.04 #> free    1.00  1.00  1.00  1.00

title: Getting started with lagprotest
text: Complete cycles. Cyclic shifting treats series one closed cycle. appropriate series spans whole cycles, 12 monthly samples annual cycle. Cyclic-shift null models can biased hold (Kalyuzhny 2020); series whose period differs length, phase-randomization surrogate (Ebisuzaki 1997) better reference. permutations. n time points 2(n − 1) cyclic permutations, smallest attainable p-value 1 / (2(n − 1) + 1), 0.043 n = 12. Corrections across many lags may unattainable α = 0.05; report raw adjusted p-values together lag profile. Different window sizes. m² lag k based n − k rows, long lags rest fewer observations. Keep candidate lags within range justified biology system. Scaling. scale = TRUE (default) variables standardized full series truncation.

what: Lagged Procrustean Randomization Test for Multivariate Time Series
title: Lagged Procrustean Randomization Test for Multivariate Time Series
text: lagprotest extends Procrustean randomization test (PROTEST) ordered multivariate series. scans Procrustes concordance two configurations across candidate temporal lags, tests lag permutation, returns lag profile, lag maximal concordance (minimum m²) per-observation Procrustes residuals. Two permutation schemes available: permutation = "cyclic" (default): cyclic shifts full series, optionally time reversal, applied lagging. keeps temporal autocorrelation null assumes series spans complete cycles (e.g., 12 monthly samples annual cycle). permutation = "free": free permutation rows within overlapping window, vegan::protest(). Rows assumed exchangeable, autocorrelated series violate; Type error can severely inflated.

title: Lagged Procrustean Randomization Test for Multivariate Time Series
Lagged Procrustean Randomization Test for Multivariate Time Series

code: library(lagprotest)  # Two 12-month series in which X leads Y by 2 months sim <- simulate_lagged_series(n_times = 12, true_lag = 2, noise_sd = 0.5,                               seed = 1)  fit <- lagged_protest(sim$X, sim$Y, lags = 0:4) fit             # lag profile, optimal lag, adjusted p-value plot(fit)       # m2 against lag, with the permutation null quantile residuals(fit)  # per-observation residuals at the optimal lag

title: Lagged Procrustean randomization test — lagged_protest
text: Rows X Y ordered time points (e.g., monthly centroids) must correspond one one. lag k > 0, X time t paired Y time t + k (X leads Y), series truncated overlapping window n - k rows. Negative lags (Y leads X) tested bidirectional = TRUE. statistic lag symmetric Procrustes sum squares \(m^2\) vegan::procrustes(); lag maximal concordance one smallest \(m^2\). Two permutation schemes available: "cyclic" (default): full Y series cyclically shifted 1, ..., n - 1 positions lagging, optionally also time-reversed (mirror = TRUE). keeps temporal autocorrelation Y null. n - 1 (2(n - 1)) shifts enumerated, nperm ignored, smallest attainable p-value 1 / (2(n - 1) + 1) (0.043 n = 12 mirror = TRUE). scheme assumes series spans complete cycles, .e., period matches number rows (e.g., 12 monthly samples annual cycle). "free": rows Y permuted random within overlapping window, vegan::protest(). assumes exchangeable rows can strongly inflate Type error series autocorrelated. P-values computed (b + 1) / (N + 1), b number permuted \(m^2\) values smaller equal observed one N number permutations, adjusted across lags stats::p.adjust(). Note \(m^2\) values different lags based different numbers rows (n - |k|).

title: lagprotest 0.1.0
text: First public release. lagged_protest() scans Procrustes concordance two ordered multivariate series across candidate lags tests lag permutation. Two schemes available: cyclic shifts full series, optionally time reversal (default), free row permutation vegan::protest(). P-values adjusted across lags. Accepts matrices, data frames dist objects (converted PCoA). print(), summary(), plot() residuals() methods lag profile, optimal lag per-observation Procrustes residuals. simulate_lagged_series() generates seasonal series AR(1) noise known lag, calibration power studies.
